title: ARR-weighted compliance triage and SLA/timeline estimator for enterprise onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and deliver an ARR-weighted compliance triage engine and customer-facing SLA/timeline estimator. The goal is to convert incoming security & compliance asks (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR, DPA, vendor questionnaires) into a ranked, time-estimated queue that accounts for commercial value, technical complexity, and legal exposure. This will enable sales and CSMs to set reliable expectations, prioritize engineering and legal resourcing, and surface exceptions that require expedited handling.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form sends structured signals to scoring engine for 90% of inbound asks (fields validated)
Scoring engine produces a triage score and a timeline estimate (days) for at least 95% of tickets without manual review
UI in Console + Sales playbook exposes top-3 reason(s) for score and the recommended lane: Fast-Track / Standard / Deferred / Exception
Benchmarked estimator accuracy: median absolute error <= 5 business days for Standard lane vs historic cases
Integration points: HubSpot ticket sync and legal Slack alerting channel are functional and tested
Sales and Legal have run 3 pilot accounts and approved the estimator outputs in >80% of trial decisions
implementation_steps: Map historical intake tickets (last 24 months) in Notion/Drive to canonical features: data residency, PHI, audit requests, contract clauses, encryption requirements
Define ARR weighting formula: base_score = feature_risk * risk_multiplier; ARR_score = base_score * log(1 + ARR_usd/100000) — experiment with multipliers
Build a lightweight scoring microservice in the intake stack that outputs: triage_score (0-100), recommended_lane, estimated_days, justification_tags
Add required fields to customer compliance intake form in Console and public intake endpoint (region, PHI presence, expected go-live, ARR band, legal stage)
Create sales-facing return payload template and CSM playbook for communicating timelines and negotiating exceptions
Instrument dashboards (Looker/Metabase) to compare predicted vs actual resolution times per lane and ARR band
Ship GitHub PR for server and Console changes, run e2e QA and pilot with three strategic accounts (Legal engaged)
Iterate scoring multipliers after pilot using regression analysis on pilot outcomes and update the estimator model
success_metrics: Average time-to-first-response for high-ARR accounts reduced from 5 business days to 1 business day
Percentage of inbound asks with a deterministic automated lane >= 85%
Sales-reported expectation accuracy >= 80% in quarterly NPS for security onboarding
Reduction in ad-hoc legal escalation pages by 30% within quarter of rollout
Correlation achieved between higher ARR bands and prioritized triage in >90% of processed tickets
risks: Over-prioritizing by ARR could create fairness concerns for smaller customers with high regulatory urgency
Estimator may under-predict time for novel or cross-team dependencies (e.g., kernel-level runtime changes for auditability)
Sales may attempt to game ARR inputs if the intake path affects deal timelines—need audit trail
Complex legal negotiations (DPA redlines) may invalidate the timeline estimator until manual review is completed
stakeholders: Engineering: Backend infra (serving runtime), Platform APIs
notes: This ticket intentionally balances revenue signals with legal exposure; final multipliers will be conservative for first release
Pilot criteria: two existing enterprise customers and one new logo in EMEA to capture regional residency cases
Keep fallback behavior: any score >= 85 and tag includes 'PHI' should auto-escalate to Legal review channel
We will version the estimator and add a rollout flag to the Console to A/B test messaging and timelines
